rounds.text: Rashi Peripherals Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of just 12.7x while delivering explosive top and bottom-line expansion [E1, E16, E19]. The company's underlying fundamentals are exceptionally robust, featuring a superior ROCE of 17.0% that easily outperforms the sector median of 12.6% [E12, E66]. Growth metrics are firing on all cylinders, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 51% and a staggering 92% surge in compounded profit growth over the same period, heavily outpacing sector medians [E16, E19, E64, E65]. This exceptional operational momentum is recognized by rules-based evaluations, which award the stock a high-confidence BUY score of 94 out of 100 [E56]. Furthermore, the market price at ₹739 vastly undercuts the DCF-derived intrinsic value of ₹2103, offering a substantial 64.9% margin of safety [E2, E39, E40]. Reverse DCF analysis highlights the extreme disconnect, showing that current market prices price in a meager 1.6% earnings growth compared to the baseline assumption of 16.0% [E41]. Conceded: borrowings have climbed to ₹2,010 Cr in Sep 2026 alongside a low cash conversion ratio of 0.40x, signaling that reported profits are currently running well ahead of cash generation [E28, E33].

Serious concerns emerge when examining the company's aggressive borrowing trajectory and cash generation quality, specifically as borrowings have more than doubled to reach ₹2,010 Cr in Sep 2026 compared to ₹991 Cr a year earlier [E33]. This massive debt accumulation is compounded by a concerning cash conversion ratio of just 0.40x for Mar 2026, which clearly indicates that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection and points to potential underlying risks in receivables or accruals [E28]. Furthermore, institutional sentiment is flashing warning signs, captured by negative money flow signals, a drop in domestic institutional holdings from 14.41% in Mar 2024 to 11.89% in Sep 2026, and recent quarter promoter selling of 0.49% [E37, E38, E54, E61]. Price performance has also raced far ahead of fundamental delivery, with the signal engine noting that recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 29% and that expectations are running hot [E51]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing sales growth of 51% alongside a low reverse DCF implied growth rate [E16, E41].

Conceded: borrowings rose to ₹2,010 Cr and cash conversion is 0.40x for Mar 2026 [E28, E33]. However, the business generated substantial liquidity with operating cash flow at ₹114 Cr and free cash flow at ₹106 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30]. While domestic institutions decreased holdings to 11.89%, foreign institutions have increased their stake to 3.99% since Mar 2024 [E36, E37]. The claim that expectations are running hot is countered by the reverse DCF, which proves the current price only prices in a modest 1.6% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 16.0% [E41]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen awards a high confidence BUY score of 94 out of 100, driven by powerful trailing sales growth of 51% and a 92% surge in compounded profit growth [E16, E19, E56].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached ₹114 Cr and free cash flow hit ₹106 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30]. However, that liquidity sits against a staggering surge in borrowings to ₹2,010 Cr in Sep 2026, more than doubling from ₹991 Cr a year earlier [E33]. The bull's reliance on foreign institutional accumulation [E36] ignores the broader institutional outflow signalled by scanX and the reduction in domestic holdings from 14.41% to 11.89% [E37, E38, E61]. Furthermore, pointing to a reverse DCF [E41] dismisses the very real operational warning of a 0.40x cash conversion ratio, which reveals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation and demanding close scrutiny of receivables and accruals [E28]. Finally, while the rules-based screen and trailing growth metrics look impressive [E16, E19, E56], promoter holding has actually decreased over the last quarter by 0.49% [E54], and the company struggles with an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend alongside a low 3-year average return on equity of 13.2% [E26, E55].

Nevertheless, foreign institutions have increased their stake to 3.99% [E36], demonstrating targeted institutional confidence that offsets broad flow signals [E38, E61]. Conceded: the cash conversion ratio sits at 0.40x for Mar 2026 [E28]. However, this is paired with actual operating cash flow of ₹114 Cr and positive free cash flow of ₹106 Cr [E29, E30]. Yet, overall promoter ownership remains exceptionally stable and high at 63.55% [E35], while the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 94 out of 100 on the back of stellar recent sales and profit growth [E56, E57, E59].

However, this isolated buying fails to negate broader institutional selling, as domestic institutions reduced their holding to 11.89% [E37] and the overall institutional money flow reads negative [E38, E61]. Nonetheless, a cash conversion ratio of 0.40x reveals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection, signaling severe risks in receivables and accruals [E28]. Yet, promoter holding actually decreased over the last quarter [E54], and the 3-year average return on equity languishes at a low 13.2% [E55]. Furthermore, borrowings nearly doubled to ₹2,010 Cr in September 2026 up from ₹991 Cr a year earlier [E33], exposing the balance sheet to aggressive leverage that high recent growth rates [E57, E59] simply cannot mask.
